patch.value: Removing an unreachable branch for coverage introduced a polynomial expression in the relation parser

The relation target parser originally took the final path segment by splitting on the separator. That form carries a branch no test can reach, because splitting a string always yields at least one element, and the coverage gate reported it. Replacing the split with a single unanchored expression that matched the final segment removed the branch and read as tidier, and it introduced a high-severity polynomial expression: the scan retries at every position in a run of separators. CodeQL flagged it on the first scan of the new repository.

The lesson is the interesting part. The change was made to satisfy a coverage gate rather than to change behaviour, and coverage pressure is exactly the pressure that produces edits nobody scrutinises as changes. It replaced a real if unreachable guard with a pattern whose cost profile nobody had considered.

The fix extracts the segment with a positional lookup whose two outcomes are both reachable, since a URL with no separator is its own final segment, and then tests that segment with an anchored pattern. Nothing is left to backtrack over, and no branch is unreachable.
The parser has no unanchored scan; both branches of the segment lookup are covered by tests that exercise them; a long run of separators is pinned by test; the code scanning alert closes
Call the relation target parser with a long run of separator characters. The unanchored form retries the match at every position.

Rewritten to extract the segment positionally and test it with an anchored pattern. Both lookup branches are reachable and covered, a sixty-four separator run is pinned, and the gate is green at 100 percent across statements, branches, functions and lines.
Closed the polynomial expression in the relation parser that a coverage edit had introduced
